findings.title: Call to non-existent zero-arg `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` fails to compile
findings.body: `UsernameForm.authenticate` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but the method defined on the superclass `UsernamePasswordForm` (line 160) has the signature `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`. This causes a compilation error (`method isConditionalPasskeysEnabled in class UsernamePasswordForm cannot be applied to given types; required: UserModel; found: no arguments`). Pass `context.getUser()` to match the superclass method signature.

findings.title: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` requires `user != null`, breaking passkey login on initial authentication
findings.body: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` returns `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`. During a normal (non-re-authentication) login, `context.getUser()` is `null` when `UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate` and `UsernamePasswordForm.challenge` run, so `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` evaluates to `false` and `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` is never called. As a result, WebAuthn conditional UI attributes and the challenge are never added to the login form on initial login, completely breaking passkey authentication when no user is pre-selected. Additionally, when `user != null` (re-authentication), this check does not verify whether that user actually has a passkey credential (`webauthnAuth.configuredFor(...)`), so passkey UI will be rendered even for users without registered passkeys when realm passkeys are enabled. The condition should allow `user == null` or check `webauthnAuth.configuredFor(context.getSession(), context.getRealm(), user)` when `user != null`.
